problem: clearPrivateView decides whether to return focus to the search field by testing whether focus is inside `.review-workspace [role="dialog"]`. This change portals the Review rules and PR watcher dialogs to document.body, so focus inside them no longer matches the selector.

finding.problem: clearPrivateView decides whether to return focus to the search field by testing whether focus is inside `.review-workspace [role="dialog"]`. This change portals the Review rules and PR watcher dialogs to document.body, so focus inside them no longer matches the selector.
finding.impact: When the board identity changes (account switch, access lost) while one of those two dialogs holds focus, the dialog unmounts and focus falls to body instead of the search field; before the change it was restored. Keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place. No data effect; narrow trigger.
finding.suggested_fix: Detect the portaled dialogs too: use overlayOpen(), or a marker class on the two dialogs, instead of an ancestor selector under .review-workspace.
finding.evidence: ReviewBoard.tsx clearPrivateView selector (unchanged line) vs createPortal(..., document.body) in ProjectReviewRules.tsx and ReviewWatcher.tsx. Read, not run. Reported independently by seven reviewers.

premise.reasoning: The ancestor selector at ReviewBoard.tsx:122 is unchanged code, and nothing at the site marks the portaled dialogs as excluded on purpose. Portaling Review rules and PR watcher to document.body (ProjectReviewRules.tsx:96, ReviewWatcher.tsx:101) is new in this branch and silently takes them out of the focus restore. overlayOpen() is already used beside it (ReviewBoard.tsx:254, 265), so the suggested fix follows the file's own pattern.

pre-existing: attentionReason itself puts the local review states (publication pending, result available) before every GitHub reason

the outdated reason ranks after live run states and closed/merged, before every GitHub-derived reason; chosen by the worker, not asked of the operator (branch-introduced, so not counted as prior intent)

premise.reasoning: The fact reproduces: reviewLane ignores outdated while laneReason returns the outdated text before attentionReason, so a Needs attention card can lose its "New reply to you" or "Review requested" reason. But the existing code already puts local review text ahead of GitHub reasons (the partial-run line), so the new placement matches a sibling. premise.question: A card in Needs attention with an outdated review shows only "Outdated review · sha", as a partial run already hides the GitHub reason. Which should the card show?
options: uphold — the lane reason (review requested, new reply, failed checks) wins, with the outdated review as a secondary line or badge
dismiss — keep local review text first, as the partial-run label already does; revisit with the stage 1 lanes

There is no signal that collapsing to identical glyphs and dropping the counts was intended; the fix makes the toolbar more consistent with that practice.
